summary: Edge keepalive reset causes truncated final choice + missing terminal metadata on streaming responses
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that when using SSE streaming through their corporate CDN that translates client HTTP/1.1->backend HTTP/2, long-running streaming requests occasionally terminate with a partial final choice and the terminal metadata (finish_reason and request_id) is missing. Impact: Client applications see partial JSON fragments and treat responses as incomplete, causing failed downstream transactions in Acme's chat reconciliation service. Occurrence: ~0.3% of streams, more frequent during peak traffic and when CDN idle-connection eviction coincides with final token flush. Environment: Private deployment, fronted by customer's CDN + our edge-proxy in us-east, requests route to dedicated serving pool. Steps to reproduce: 1) Client opens SSE stream with prompt causing ~10-12s generation. 2) Simulate CDN idle eviction by forcing TCP FIN/RST (or wait ~90s idle). 3) Observe client receives normal streaming chunks but final "end" JSON containing metadata is truncated or never arrives. Observed behavior: stream body closes mid-json or a short keepalive-only chunk is the last item; no finish_reason and request_id in logs at customer side. Server-side logs show final payload emitted but a downstream HTTP/2 stream reset (RST_STREAM) often appears in same window. Expected behavior: complete terminal event with choice and metadata should arrive; platform should gracefully re-deliver or signal resume token so client can resume and re-request tail. Logs and traces: edge-proxy trace IDs provided below (see investigation notes). Additional notes: Issue reproduced with both SSE and websocket fallback when the edge performs an early connection termination during stream finalization.
investigation_notes: 03/10 15:22 - SRE (Diego): Pulled tcpdump from edge-proxy (trace id ep-20260310-0157). Observed RST_STREAM frames originating from CDN IP immediately after server sent final chunk. Serving-runtime logs show final choice serialized and queued for flush at t=+11.2s. 03/11 09:14 - Hypothesis: HTTP/2 stream state transitions + edge keepalive/idle eviction can race with final flush; edge may coalesce final bytes into a buffer then receive a connection-level GOAWAY/RST from upstream CDN causing bytes to be dropped before being forwarded to the client HTTP/1.1 connection. 03/11 13:30 - Reproduced in lab by injecting an artificial RST right after last write; client received truncated JSON (missing trailing metadata). 03/11 17:05 - Verified websocket fallback sometimes preserves terminal metadata if the proxy flush path is synchronous; inconsistency correlates with proxy write buffer size and timing. Traces: ep-20260310-0157, ep-20260311-0928. Tentative root cause: edge-proxy does not guarantee atomic flush of terminal event when upstream connection is reset; in HTTP/2 translation path a reset can drop trailing bytes without retrying or re-framing terminal event for client. Related: similar symptom in SUP-219210 (session token swap) but different trigger.
resolution: Workarounds provided: (1) Customer: enable short SSE keepalive pings from client (every 10s) to avoid CDN idle eviction; (2) Customer: pin to websocket fallback for critical flows while we roll a fix; (3) Support: temporary upstream config toggle to reduce proxy write coalescing (performed 2026-03-11 20:00 UTC). Engineering fix plan: Edge-proxy change to flush terminal events synchronously and treat terminal writes as high-priority flushes; add a small retry window where if a RST/GOAWAY is observed during terminal write, edge will try to re-emit terminal frame over a fresh connection or signal a resume token. Owners: Edge team (Diego), Serving-runtime (Lena Patel). Rollout plan: implement patch -> internal canary -> 2-stage prod rollout across us-east/us-west (ETA for start 2026-03-18). Post-release verification: create synthetic runner that opens SSE streams and asserts final metadata received, add alert for partial-terminal rate >0.05%. Follow-ups: update streaming runbook with guidance and add automatic detection on Console for partial-terminal events.
